points.why: Explicitly frames the test as the 8-point margin over the 10% target and defines mattering as pushing that margin below zero.
Describes one-at-a-time swings with ±25% default, holding others fixed, a tornado chart against the margin with a zero line, and identifying inputs that cross it.
Notes one-at-a-time misses inputs that matter together and recommends Morris screening or Sobol indices when runs are cheap.
Concludes with a short measure/skip list of usually 2–4 inputs and a re-scoped quote rather than collecting all 14.

notes: The Sobol claim that S1 tells you how much uncertainty disappears if you measure an input is a slight oversimplification (it assumes measuring removes all uncertainty), but it is not harmful.
